study.title: Brain Functional Interaction of Acupuncture Effects in Diarrhea-Dominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome
study.study_design: Prospective study with pre-post design; IBS-D patients scanned before and after acupuncture stimulation, compared with normal controls
study.population: Diarrhea-dominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D) patients and age-matched normal controls
study.inclusion_criteria: (a) age between 18 and 55 years old, (b) IBS-SSS above 75 on baseline, (c) no drug treatment within 2 weeks, (d) no history of acupuncture stimulation within 3 months related to IBS, and (e) no participation in other clinical research projects
study.exclusion_criteria: (a) other IBS subtypes, (b) organic gastrointestinal disease or history of gastrointestinal surgery, (c) other confounding medical conditions (such as diabetes, hyperthyroidism, mental illness, and other chronic pains), (d) serious heart, liver, and kidney illness, (e) pregnant or lactating women, (f) vivo magnetic implants (such as iron, or with cochlear implants, vascular clips, or with pacemaker), and (g) metal sensitivity or afraid of needle

arms.dropouts: 2 excluded due to inconsistent scanning parameters
IBS-D patients who did not undergo acupuncture stimulation (baseline scan only); overall 43 enrolled, 24 finally included after exclusions
5 patients who received acupuncture stimulation were excluded due to inconsistent scan parameters

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI; subjects instructed to keep as still as possible and not to think systematically

conditions.timepoint_exact: First scan at diagnosis, before any acupuncture stimulation
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI; subjects instructed to keep as still as possible and not to think systematically

conditions.condition_label_exact: IBS-D post-acupuncture scan (after 6 weeks of acupuncture stimulation)
conditions.timepoint_exact: Second scan after undergoing all acupuncture stimulations (6 consecutive weeks)
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI; subjects instructed to keep as still as possible and not to think systematically

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Acupuncture stimulation at seven acupuncture points
interventions.stimulation_type: manual acupuncture with lifting, thrusting and twirling manipulation
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: DU20 and EX-HN3 on head; ST36, ST37, SP6 on lower limbs; ST25 on abdomen; LR3 on foot
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral for Bai Hui (DU20); bilateral implied for paired points
interventions.needle_size_exact: diameter of 0.3 mm and a length of 40 mm
interventions.depth_exact: DU20: 0.5–0.8 cun obliquely; EX-HN3: 0.2–0.3 cun obliquely; ST36, ST37, SP6: 1 cun; ST25: 1–1.5 cun; LR3: 0.5 cun
interventions.manipulation_exact: lifting, thrusting and twirling; needles manipulated twice every 10 min with intermittent stimulation, intermittent stimulation lasted for 10 s
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Yes; optimal acupuncture response named Deqi (a sensation of soreness, numbness, fullness, and heaviness, and/or adjacent muscle twitching)
interventions.needle_retention_exact: 30 min before being pulled out in each session
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: every other day (up to three times a week) for 6 consecutive weeks
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: Acupuncturists with more than 6 years of clinical experience
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Acupuncture could modulate hypothalamus-limbic systems; gastrointestinal dysfunction caused by IBS might be associated with disorders of hypothalamus-limbic nervous systems; acupoints determined according to the point localization method issued by the World Health Organization (WHO)

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: Deqi (a sensation of soreness, numbness, fullness, and heaviness, and/or adjacent muscle twitching)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was intended and described as achieved but no quantitative data were reported for deqi sensations

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: SIEMENS Veno 3-Tesla scanner with 18-channel phased-array head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: EPI sequence for functional images; T1-weighted sagittal three-dimensional magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) sequence for structural images
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Volume numbers = 210, 42 axial slices for each data volume
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space using echo-planar imaging (EPI) template
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel with a full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of 4 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Head motion correction was executed; Friston 24 motion parameters, white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid signals were regressed
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: Friston 24 motion parameters, white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid signals were regressed; GM tissue of each subject utilized to mask corresponding fMRI data

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included in this study. All IBS-D patients received verum acupuncture. There is no sham comparison.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding assessments were not reported. The paper does not mention any measure of participant expectancy or treatment credibility.
Deqi was intended but no quantitative deqi scale data (e.g., MASS scores) were reported. Only narrative description of intended Deqi sensation is provided.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the paper.
No trial registration number is reported.

The IBSbs group and IBS1st group appear to be the same 24 patients scanned before and after acupuncture (within-subject design), not two separate independent cohorts. This is inferred from the methods describing that 24 IBS-D patients were included and those who underwent acupuncture were scanned again. However, the paper sometimes treats them as separate groups in comparisons.

Table 1 reports standard errors (SE) in parentheses, not standard deviations (SD). The header says 'standard errors in parentheses.' Values for IBS-SSS, IBS-QOL, HAMA, Age, and Years of Education are reported as mean (SE).

Figure 3 shows disorder functional connections with * (Bonferroni corrected) and # (uncorrected p < 0.05) marks. The HIP.R–IFGoperc.L connection (Figure 3A) shows * for IBSbs vs NC comparison; SOG.R–LING.L (Figure 3B) and Vermis12–Cerebelum45.L (Figure 3C) show # (uncorrected). This distinction was preserved in extraction.

The paper labels the disorder FC analysis for HIP.R–MOG.L (Figure 4A), SOG.R–MOG.L (Figure 4B), and vermis6–Cerebelum9.R (Figure 4C) as both 'disorder' and 'cured' functional connections — they appear in both the disorder FC section (section 3.2) and the cured FC section (section 3.3). Both aspects were extracted separately.

No MNI coordinates are reported anywhere in the paper for any brain regions. All results are described using region labels from the AAL atlas without coordinate tables. No neuroimaging coordinate tables were present.

The paper does not report global network metrics (global efficiency, global clustering coefficient, path length, small-world index) for individual groups. Only states global brain functional interaction and segregation were not affected by acupuncture stimulation.

The number of sessions for acupuncture is described as 'every other day (up to three times a week) for 6 consecutive weeks' but a precise total number of sessions is not given numerically (implying approximately 18 sessions maximum).

The LOOCV ROC AUC values reported in Figure 10 captions (0.72, 0.69, 0.67, 0.71) are read from figure labels in the paper. The classification accuracy values (73.2%, 70.8%, 69.4%, 72.6%) are stated in the text. These are preserved as reported.

For the activated functional connections (Figure 6), the STG.R–cerebelum8.R connection shows # (p < 0.05 uncorrected) marks, while ORBsup.L–LING.R shows * (Bonferroni corrected) marks. This distinction is preserved in extraction.
The paper does not report whether the comfort, diet, and lifestyle consultation provided alongside acupuncture could confound the neural or clinical results. This is not controlled for.
The sparsity analysis (Figure 2) reports descriptive observations about frequency connection matrices but no formal statistical comparison is reported for the sparsity differences between groups.
The paper uses Fisher's z transformation of Pearson correlations for FC calculation, but does not specify the bandpass filtering parameters applied to resting-state fMRI data prior to FC analysis.
